spatial_claims.claim: Rectangles applied to AC producing breadths AH and KH; remaining piece MK equals twice rect(AG,GD). Standard application-of-areas construction.
Sum of squares on AG, GD applied to AC produces rational breadth SN commensurable in length with AC.
Twice rect(AG,GD) applied to AC produces breadth NQ rational and incommensurable in length with AC.
Semicircle described on SQ = SN + NQ with perpendicular from N meeting semicircle at P; determines lines OP and PQ.

configuration_map: All geometric constructions are computational devices for algebraic operations on irrational magnitudes: (1) Application of areas to line AC in Steps 3-6 lays out rectangles along a line to represent products and quotients — a one-dimensional arrangement with no ambiguity. (2) The semicircle construction in Step 10 is a standard well-defined construction for finding mean proportionals. No points are claimed inside or outside figures, no rays are ordered relative to each other, and no angles are decomposed in a geometrically significant sense. The entire argument concerns commensurability relations between irrational magnitudes.
